pages.title: The Visit
pages.content:
An inspection hour is 60 minutes with 2 technicians and 5 stops: the landing, the car, the pit, the machine and the lobby. They fill a 32-point checklist on paper, and the written report follows in 2 working days.

Arrive, inspect, report

Minutes 0–10: meet the building manager, sign in, stand the notice at the landing and take the lift out of service. Minutes 10–50: the five stops and the checklist. Minutes 50–60: return the lift to service and go through the findings on paper.

Book an inspection

pages.title: Buildings
pages.content:
Noboru Lifts works with facilities managers and owners of office buildings of 4 to 12 floors.

Alder House, Foundry Court, Meridian Yard

Alder House has 9 floors and 2 lifts; a door that hesitated on floor 6 was traced to a worn sill guide. Foundry Court has 6 floors and 1 lift and got its first written record. Meridian Yard has 12 floors and 3 lifts, inspected one at a time across two mornings.

Book an inspection

pages.title: Fees
pages.content:
All prices are in USD and exclude tax. The 32-point checklist and the written report are included in the inspection hour. An inspection hour is not a statutory examination.

Inspection hour, first lift: $240. Each further lift, same visit: $140. Door adjustment visit: $320. Monthly service agreement, per lift: $190 / month. Fault call-out, within call-out hours: $280. Written second opinion on a quote: $180.

Book an inspection

pages.title: About
pages.content:
Noboru Lifts began in 2011 at 14 Wharf Row, Easterhaven. Ines Varga founded the company and still leads inspections. Seven people work from Wharf Row.

The day starts at 06:30. Vans are out by 06:40, the first lift is out of service at 07:00, reports are written in the afternoon and the second round begins at 18:00.

posts.title: What a paper checklist catches
posts.excerpt: Why the 32 points are filled in by hand at the lift, and what that slows down in a good way.
posts.content:
The 32-point checklist is paper. It is filled in at the lift, at the stop where each point belongs, by whichever of the two technicians is standing there. Nothing is left to memory in the van.

Paper is slow in a useful way. A point that is not filled in is visible as a blank, and a blank on the sheet is read out loud in the last ten minutes, with the building manager listening.

posts.title: Why we start at seven
posts.excerpt: The first lift is out of service at 07:00, before the building fills.
posts.content:
The day starts at 06:30 at 14 Wharf Row. Vans leave by 06:40, and the first lift is taken out of service at 07:00, while the lobby is still quiet.

A second round begins at 18:00. Both are one-hour slots, Monday to Friday, outside the building’s busy times.

posts.title: Reading an old lift’s logbook
posts.excerpt: What a thin logbook still tells you about a lift that has run for years.
posts.content:
Some office lifts have run for years with almost nothing on file. A thin logbook is still a record: dates, a name, a note about a door.

The inspection hour adds the next page, written down at the five stops and handed back to the manager.
